name: Help Scout
subcategory: help desks, live chat and support knowledge
tagline: Manage a shared email inbox and compact help center for a small team

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 5 users; 1 inbox; 1 Docs site; 100 contacts/month; 10 saved replies; 10 tags
tiers.notes: Also limited to 10 Docs articles, 1 Beacon and 30 days of reporting history.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: Up to 25 users; 2 included inboxes; 2 Docs sites; unlimited contacts; 1 basic SLA; 2 years reporting history
tiers.notes: Official pricing page displayed the annual effective rate; its monthly toggle did not expose a retrievable current USD rate.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Up to 50 users; 5 inboxes; 3 Docs sites; 5 light users included (25 maximum); 2 advanced SLAs; all-time reporting
tiers.notes: Official pricing page displayed the annual effective rate; its monthly toggle did not expose a retrievable current USD rate.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited users with 10-user minimum; 10 inboxes; 5 Docs sites; 15 light users included (50 maximum); unlimited SLAs
tiers.notes: Official pricing page displayed the annual effective rate; its monthly toggle did not expose a retrievable current USD rate.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Up to 5 users, 1 inbox, 1 Docs site, 100 contacts/month, 10 saved replies, 10 tags, 10 articles, 1 Beacon and 30 days of report history
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (pricing page states annual is 16% cheaper; annual rates shown above)
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI Answers is $0.75 per resolved AI session after a 3-month free trial. More than 2,000 proactive-message viewers/month starts at $20. Extra inboxes cost $12/month or $10/month annual; extra Docs sites $24/$20; extra light users $12/$10. Pro has a 10-paid-user minimum.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Help Scout, manage a shared email inbox and compact help center for a small team. The hard boundary is email threading, customer context, docs, workflows, reporting, and support polish, plus channel integrations and support operations.
coreLoopDIY: Receive customer messages into a shared team inbox, reply from one place, maintain a compact help center, and retain a searchable conversation history.
whatYouLose: email threading, customer context, docs, workflows, reporting, and support polish
ongoingBurden: message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Help Scout because support software survives because missing or misrouting one customer message is expensive and every channel behaves differently. The recurring cost buys message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Chatwoot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source customer engagement and shared-inbox platform.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: A proper support inbox with chat, email and a help center; free software, billable server chores.

facts.install: Docker Compose on a Linux VM, followed by environment, database, reverse-proxy and TLS configuration
facts.dataFormat: Application data in PostgreSQL, queues/cache in Redis, and attachments on local disk or S3-compatible/cloud object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Chatwoot is broader and self-hosted, but its email conversation experience and Beacon-style polish are less focused than Help Scout's.
facts.setupBlocker: Provisioning a Linux server and correctly wiring DNS/TLS, SMTP, PostgreSQL/Redis and storage

alternatives.name: Frappe Helpdesk
alternatives.desc: Tickets, SLAs and a knowledge base in a clean Frappe shell; the five-minute installer still leaves you the pager.

facts.install: Run Frappe's easy-install script against the stable container image on a Linux server
facts.dataFormat: Tickets in the Frappe site database, with public and private attachments in the site's files directories
facts.gapVsPaid: Its integrations, reporting and customer-facing polish are less mature than Help Scout's, while the server remains yours.
facts.setupBlocker: A Linux server, domain/DNS, Docker or the easy-install script, and mail account configuration

alternatives.name: osTicket
alternatives.desc: Email and web forms become assigned tickets; dated, dependable and very much your PHP server.

facts.install: Upload the release to a PHP web root, create a MySQL database, then finish the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Tickets and configuration in MySQL; attachments in the database or server filesystem depending on storage setup; ticket metadata can export as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: The dated ticket interface is a clear step down from Help Scout's conversational mailbox and compact Docs experience.
facts.setupBlocker: A PHP/MySQL web host plus database credentials, filesystem permissions and mail piping or IMAP setup

alternatives.name: Zammad
alternatives.desc: A serious ticket desk with email, chat, SLAs and a knowledge base; setup is the first ticket.

facts.install: Deploy the Docker Compose/Portainer stack or install supported Linux packages
facts.dataFormat: Ticket and user data in PostgreSQL, search indexes in Elasticsearch, and attachments/backups in Docker volumes or server storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its heavy infrastructure and ticket semantics are less approachable than Help Scout's small-team inbox.
facts.setupBlocker: A comparatively large server and familiarity with Docker/Portainer, PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch

alternatives.name: tawk.to
alternatives.desc: Live chat, tickets, email, and a help centre for zero dollars; the tiny tawk.to badge pays the rent.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then paste the generated JavaScript widget or install a CMS plugin
facts.dataFormat: Chats, tickets and contacts in tawk.to's cloud account; chat and ticket exports are JSON
facts.gapVsPaid: Ticketing and help content are secondary to live chat, so the shared-email and docs experience is less refined than Help Scout's.
facts.setupBlocker: Access to edit the website or install its CMS plugin

alternatives.name: Odoo Helpdesk One App Free
alternatives.desc: A real hosted ticket desk for unlimited users, as long as Helpdesk is your one free Odoo app.

facts.install: Hosted Odoo Online signup with Helpdesk selected as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: An Odoo Online PostgreSQL database in Odoo's cloud, with record exports and downloadable ZIP database backups
facts.gapVsPaid: The one-app-free constraint and broad Odoo shell are less focused and less personable than Help Scout.

rejectedAlternatives.name: FreeScout
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The shared inbox is free, but its knowledge base is a paid module, so it misses the stated job.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Freshdesk Free Program
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free program lasts six months, which is not an indefinite alternative.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Zoho Desk Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The inbox is free for three agents; the public knowledge base is a paid feature.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Standard plan and a small-team shared inbox DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Help Scout in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: receive customer messages into a shared team inbox, reply from one place, maintain a compact help center, and retain a searchable conversation history.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one workspace, agents, contacts, inboxes, conversations, messages, labels, and assignment.
Provide a website chat widget with reconnect, unread counts, file limits, and clear availability state.
Create a shared inbox with filters, collision warnings, notes, canned replies, and searchable history.
Add email notifications, browser notifications, and an immutable assignment and status log.
Implement spam controls, attachment scanning hooks, retention settings, export, and contact deletion.
Ship Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, and a documented admin recovery flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out many social and messaging channels.
Deliberately leave out AI agents trained on proprietary support data.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workforce management, SSO, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
